As a Black Female anime fan who has been watching anime since I was a young child, I do not belive so but I found this article(http://www.vice.com/read/what-black-anime-fans-can-teach-us-about-race-in-america-805)) and I was wondering if there where any black anime fans who agree with this article and their reasons or their reasons for not agreeing. Replies a greatly welcomed :)

I'm not Black, but I hope you won't mind my take on this.

My issue with that article is that a good part of its content is predicated on a moronic, false notion.

A lot of anime characters read as white.

Not only is this fucking stupid, its patently false. In surveys of viewers, responses have shown that different demographics view characters differently, but in the primary target demographic (read: Japanese viewers), they are almost always interpreted as Japanese. Characters have Japanese personality tropes and mannerisms, and are often written with mindsets that reflect Japanese society in some fashion or another, elements of the Japanese cultural zeitgeist show up in the content, etc. One could probably go so far as to say anime is primarily made by Japanese people for Japanese people (duh).

I would suggest instead that anime characters are effectively human simulacra which allow viewers to identify or interpose their own traits and values with the character to some degree or another which both adds to why anime can appeal to so many different types of viewers, as well as helping to explain why brain-damaged comments like the one quoted above can get made in the first place. I think the very fact that there are anime fans who are so diverse, be it Black, Indonesian, Latino, or whatever else, indicates that there's not a single universal way in which characters are viewed or interpreted.

Instead of saying that the characters read as white, they should say that the characters could be read as white while they can't be read as black.

Anime characters are usually too stylized to be read as one single race.

I would agree with that, although I would disagree with any suggestion that there's ill intent or nefarious intentions behind it.

I've no doubt that some fans have experienced negativity for issues like this, but I think that's a people being narrow-minded problem, rather than an anime problem.

I don't think there's necessarily any ill intent either.

Caucasian and Asian people just happen to look quite similar when you remove factors such as hair color.

I don't think you can read (most) anime characters as "white." I guess you can read them as racially white because they tend to have light skin, and other racial markers are lost in artstyle, but they are most certainly ethnically Japanese.

Of course, this is just anecdotal observation, so take that with as many grains of salt as you need. Male black anime fans suffer the same problems of just general male nerdity. Female black anime fans have to deal with the hellhole of catty cliques on top of nerdity.
